slides.title: Reporting Cash Payments of Over $10,000
slides.description:
If, in a 12 month period, you receive more than $10,000 in cash from one buyer as a result of a transaction in your dealership, you MUST report it to the IRS and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) on form 8300.

What Payments Must Be Reported?

You must file form 8300 to report cash paid to you if it is:

  1. Over $10,000
  2. Received as:
    1. One lump sum of over $10,000
    2. Installment payments that causes the total cash received within 1 year of the initial payment to total more than $10,000 or
    3. Other previously unreported payments that cause the total cash received within a 12 month period to total more than $10,000
  3. Received in the course of your trade or business.
  4. Received from the same buyer (or agent) and
  5. Received in a single or in related transactions.

slides.title: Reporting Cash Payments of Over $10,000
slides.description:
What Is Cash?

Cash is:

  1. The coins and currency of the United States (and any other country) and
  2. A cashier’s check, bank draft, traveler’s check or money order you receive, if it has a face value of $10,000 or less and you receive it in:
    1. A designated reporting transaction (the retail sale of a consumer durable such as an automobile or boat), or
    2. Any transaction in which you know the payer is trying to avoid the reporting of the transaction on Form 8300.

Note. Cash may include a cashiers check even if it is called a “treasurers check” or a “bank check”

Cash does not include a check drawn on an individuals personal account.

What Is A Related Transaction?

Any transaction between a buyer ( or agent of buyer) and a seller that occur within a 24 hour period are related transactions. If you receive $10,000 or more in cash during 2 or more transactions from one buyer in a 24 hour period, you must treat the transactions as one transaction and report the payments on Form 8300.

The reporting requirement also applies for currency received in a period exceeding 24 hours if you have reason to know that these are related transactions.

slides.title: Reporting Cash Payments of Over $10,000
slides.description:
What About Suspicious Transactions?

If you receive $10,000 or less in cash, you may voluntarily file Form 8300 if the transaction appears to be suspicious. A transaction is suspicious if it appears that a person is trying to cause you not to file the Form 8300, or is trying to cause you to file a false or incomplete Form 8300, or if there is a sign of possible illegal activity.

If you are suspicious, you are encouraged to call the local IRS Criminal Investigation Division ASAP or you can call toll free

1-800-800-2877

slides.title: Reporting Cash Payments of Over $10,000
slides.description:
When Should You File Form 8300?

Generally, you must file Form 8300 within 15 days after receiving a payment.

More than 1 payment.If the first payment is not more than $10,000, you must add the first payment and any later payments made within one year of the first payment. When the total cash payments are more than $10,000, you must file Form 8300 within 15 days.

After you file Form 8300, you must start a new count of cash payments received from that buyer. If you receive more than $10,000 in additional cash payments from that buyer within a 12 month period, you must file another Form 8300 within 15 days of the payment that causes the cash total to be more than $10,000

Where Should Form 8300 Be Filed?

Mail the form to the address given in the Form 8300 instructions.

Required Statement To Buyer

You must give a written or electronic statement to each person named on any Form 8300 that you file.

You can give the statement electronically only if the person agrees to receive it in that format. The statement must show the name and address of the dealership, the name and phone number of a contact person, and the total amount of reportable cash you received from that person during that year. You must also state that you are reporting this information to the IRS. You must send the statement by January 31st of the year following the year that you received the cash that caused you to file the form.

slides.title: Reporting Cash Payments of Over $10,000
slides.description:
Penalties

There are civil penalties for failure to:

  • File a correct Form 8300 by the date it is due.
  • Provide the required statement to those named in the Form 8300.

If you intentionally disregarded the requirement to file the correct Form 8300 by the date it is due, the penalty is the larger of:

  1. $25,000, or
  2. The amount of cash you received and were required to report (up to $100,000).

There are criminal penalties for;

  • Willful failure to file Form 8300,
  • Willfully filing a false or fraudulent Form 8300,
  • Stopping, or trying to stop Form 8300 from being filed, and
  • Setting up, or helping to set up a transaction in a way that would make it seem unnecessary to file Form 8300.

If you willfully fail to file Form 8300, you can be fined up to $250,000 ($500,000 for corporations) or sentenced to up to 5 years in prison, or both. The penalties for failure to file may also apply to any person (including a payer) who attempts to interfere with or prevent the seller from filing a correct Form 8300.
